terminos.definicion: A professional who helps assess soil, crops and local conditions. They should review recommendations before planting decisions are made.
The ability of crops to cope with adverse conditions. The tool compares their estimated response to frost, water shortages and temperatures outside their suitable range.
High: a pilot site with satellite data. Medium: climate adjusted with SENAMHI data. Low: NASA POWER only, without local correction.
A sequence of different crops and fallow periods on the same plot over several growing seasons.
A period of water shortage. In the calendar, the indicator measures how far mean monthly rainfall falls below 60 mm; it is not a drought probability.
Height above sea level, in meters. The tool is intended for areas at or above 2,500 meters.
The loss of fertile soil carried away by rainfall, especially on uncovered slopes.
Approximate values that still require validation. Current crop parameters are team estimates and should be reviewed with a local agronomist.
Plants or plant parts used to feed livestock. In the tool’s score, this criterion also includes an income estimate.
A temperature drop that can freeze water and damage crops. The app uses air temperatures below 2 °C as a preventive risk signal, not as confirmation of freezing on the plot.

For a given month, the share of analyzed years with at least one day below 2 °C minimum air temperature. The app uses this threshold as a risk signal at every point. It uses 2 °C rather than 0 °C because soil and plants can become colder than air measured 2 meters above ground.
The share of the soil surface protected by plants or crop residues. It helps reduce erosion.
High temperatures that may affect crops. In the calendar, this indicator increases when monthly mean temperature exceeds 24 °C; it is not a probability of damage.
A coordinate indicating how far north or south a place is. Negative values are south of the equator.
NASA data are adjusted using SENAMHI data, which better represent the highland climate.
A coordinate indicating how far east or west a place is. Peru uses negative values, west of the Greenwich meridian.
A NASA service providing historical climate data. The tool retrieves temperature and rainfall for the selected point; they represent a grid cell, not an exact measurement of your plot.
A satellite indicator of vegetation greenness. In general, a higher value indicates more green vegetation.
Plants such as faba bean, Andean lupin and vetch associate with bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen. Returning residues can add nitrogen to the soil and reduce fertilizer needs.
A location for which the team prepares additional local data. Cajamarca has climate corrections based on SENAMHI PISCO.
A piece of land used for farming. In this tool, it is represented by the point you select on the map.
The importance you assign to each criterion. Sliders range from 0, not important, to 5, very important; these values affect the final score.
A chart comparing monthly frost, low rainfall and heat indicators based on historical climate. It is not a weather forecast.

A value from 0 to 100 combining the five criteria according to your priorities. A higher value indicates a better match within this comparison; it is not a yield percentage or harvest guarantee. If all priorities are 0, criteria have equal weight.
Satellite data represent an area. A field measurement describes a specific point, such as a weather station.
A climate dataset developed by SENAMHI from weather stations and other data. It is used to adjust NASA POWER temperatures and rainfall in Cajamarca.
The ability of soil to support crops. The tool estimates it from nitrogen inputs and ground cover.
Indicates whether soil is wetter or drier than usual for that location and time of year.
Surface inclination, expressed as a percentage. A 20 % slope rises 20 meters per 100 horizontal meters. If no data are available, the engine uses an estimate of 18 %.
When rainfall in a month does not meet the crop’s needs at that stage.
A criterion that favors crops with lower estimated water needs per growing season. The score does not indicate liters saved or guarantee sufficient rainfall.
